research_basis.authoring_method: Original synthesis using the user brief and the THE DMI implementation reference as the structural benchmark.
research_basis.licence_handling: Original implementation content informed by Jisc structure. Jisc digital maturity materials are published under terms including CC BY-NC-SA on the main toolkit page; scenarios and practitioner language here are independently written.
notes: The source brief describes a 3-level model and requests 10 boundaries. This implementation therefore operationalises the two assessable adjacent boundaries in a 3-level model: Established to Enhanced (EM) and Enhanced to Mature (MM).
The brief also mentioned EE as a target-level code; that label is retained in metadata as an entry-threshold alias rather than a scored boundary.

objects.stem: Your institution is dealing with the following situation: a university trying to move from isolated pilots to a common transformation narrative. Which next step best reflects stronger Organisational Digital Culture?

response_options.text: Continue relying on local champions and collect examples of good practice, but avoid tighter cross-institution coordination for now.
response_options.nuisance_reason: Visible progress is real, but coordination remains too weak for the higher boundary.

response_options.text: Assign shared ownership, align expectations across units, and use evidence from multiple areas to coordinate the next phase.
Embed the area into mainstream planning, review cycles, and external benchmarking as a normal institutional capability.

objects.discrimination_notes: This scenario isolates the EM boundary in Organisational Digital Culture by contrasting a lower-side response, the threshold response, and a higher-side or overshoot response.
